onchain.event_schema:
The OrderFilled signature CHANGED between V1 and V2 — using the V1 schema against V2 logs returns nothing.

=== V2 (current; src/exchange/mixins/Events.sol in ctf-exchange-v2) ===
event OrderFilled(
    bytes32 indexed orderHash,
    address indexed maker,
    address indexed taker,
    uint8   side,              // 0 = BUY, 1 = SELL (Side enum)
    uint256 tokenId,           // <-- the ERC1155 positionId == our clobTokenId
    uint256 makerAmountFilled,
    uint256 takerAmountFilled,
    uint256 fee,
    bytes32 builder,
    bytes32 metadata
);
topic0 = 0xd543adfd945773f1a62f74f0ee55a5e3b9b1a28262980ba90b1a89f2ea84d8ee
Indexed topics: [topic0, orderHash, maker(addr in last 20 bytes), taker].
Non-indexed data words (32 bytes each, in order): [0]=side, [1]=tokenId, [2]=makerAmountFilled, [3]=takerAmountFilled, [4]=fee, [5]=builder, [6]=metadata.

V2 OrdersMatched(bytes32,address,uint8,uint256,uint256,uint256) topic0 = 0x174b3811690657c217184f89418266767c87e4805d09680c39fc9c031c0cab7c. V2 also emits FeeCharged(address,uint256). Each match emits TWO OrderFilled legs: the maker leg (side=0) and the taker leg (side=1) with makerAmountFilled/takerAmountFilled swapped — so raw-log fill count is ~2x distinct trades.

=== V1 (legacy, pre-2026-04-28; orderbook-subgraph ExchangeMapping.ts) ===
event OrderFilled(bytes32 indexed orderHash, address indexed maker, address indexed taker, uint256 makerAssetId, uint256 takerAssetId, uint256 makerAmountFilled, uint256 takerAmountFilled, uint256 fee);
topic0 = 0xd0a08e8c493f9c94f29311604c9de1b4e8c8d4c06bd0c789af57f2d65bfec0f6 (DIFFERENT). V1 used makerAssetId/takerAssetId pairs (one side == 0 meaning USDC); V2 collapsed this into one tokenId + a side flag.

PRICE & SIZE (V2): one leg of the pair is USDC (6dp), the other is shares of `tokenId` (6dp). For side=0 (BUY): usdc=makerAmountFilled/1e6, shares=takerAmountFilled/1e6, price=makerAmountFilled/takerAmountFilled. For side=1 (SELL): usdc=takerAmountFilled/1e6, shares=makerAmountFilled/1e6, price=takerAmountFilled/makerAmountFilled. price is that token's own price; YES_price + NO_price = 1.00 (verified: NO @ 0.51 alongside YES @ 0.49 in the same tx). fee is in USDC base units (6dp), 0 on many legs.
onchain.best_public_route:
Ranking for a 5-min-window backfill, no API key:

1. PUBLIC POLYGON RPC eth_getLogs (BEST, and the ONLY one that actually reaches our window).
   - Endpoint that worked, no key: https://1rpc.io/matic  (also publicnode/drpc exist but timed out on log queries; 1rpc was fast: 5-block call 0.36s, 50-block calls fine).
   - Pros: hits the live V2 chain directly, so it has the post-2026-04-28 data the subgraphs lack. This IS the user's "every order is on the blockchain" ground truth.
   - Cons: 1rpc caps eth_getLogs at 50 blocks/call (hard error -32602 above 50). Our 5-min window is ~150 blocks (Polygon ~2.05s/block), so 3 paginated calls per window. Must first map timestamp->block (block-by-number binary search, or use a block explorer's getblocknobytime). tokenId is in data not topics, so you cannot server-side-filter by token — you fetch all OrderFilled on the exchange contract and filter client-side. High-throughput windows return ~3,700 logs per 50 blocks. Free public RPCs are rate-limited and flaky; for many windows rotate endpoints or accept retries.

2. GOLDSKY PUBLIC SUBGRAPH (orderbook-subgraph) — DEAD for our use case.
   - Endpoint live and returns valid JSON, but the indexer is FROZEN at block 87814766 / last OrderFilledEvent timestamp 1777374040 = 2026-04-28 11:00 UTC, exactly the V1->V2 migration. It only ever indexed the V1 exchanges and was abandoned at cutover. Every version probed (0.0.1, prod = 2026-04-28; 0.0.2 = 2025-08; resync/prod = 2026-01) is stale; 0.0.3-1.0.0 = 404. Our window (2026-06-18) is 51 days inside the un-indexed gap, so it returns [] for our tokens. Great for pre-2026-04-28 history, useless after. No key needed but no data.

3. DUNE — viable but not no-key/no-friction. Free tier needs an account+API key, has credit limits, and you depend on whether Dune's spellbook has decoded the new V2 exchange (the migration is recent). Good for ad-hoc SQL over many windows once set up, not for a key-free script. Not tested here (would need a key).

Verdict: for post-migration windows, eth_getLogs against 0xE111...996B (binary) / 0xe222...310F59 (negrisk) via 1rpc.io is the only working key-free route.
onchain.token_id_mapping:
DIRECT IDENTITY — no transformation needed. The uint256 `tokenId` in the V2 OrderFilled event data word [1] is byte-for-byte the ERC1155 positionId, which is exactly our clobTokenId interpreted as a decimal integer.

Proven: querying the CTF V2 exchange (0xE111...996B) over our window and comparing data-word[1] against our known
  yes_token = 64167396574280389277007219975075054246310340364325837958986723157864686716857
  no_token  = 21863015595224424904547871213526079602937693638643749884737061528844328418597
matched 224 of 454 logs in a 5-block slice (and ~3,861 of ~7,383 across 100 blocks). The other logs are other markets sharing the same exchange contract in those blocks.

So: clobTokenId (decimal string from CLOB API) -> int() -> compare to event tokenId. On V1 the same value lived in makerAssetId OR takerAssetId (whichever side wasn't 0/USDC); on V2 it's the single `tokenId` field. The positionId itself is keccak-derived from (collateral, collectionId) per Gnosis CTF, but you never need to recompute it — the CLOB clobTokenIds ARE the positionIds.
onchain.feasibility:
Honest verdict: the on-chain route is REAL and is genuine ground truth — the user's thesis ("every order is recorded on the blockchain") is correct for fills: every executed match emits an OrderFilled log on the exchange contract, and we proved we can read them with no API key for our exact window. BUT it is materially more work than data-api /trades, and for backfilling many windows /trades is the pragmatic winner.

Why on-chain is heavier:
- No subgraph shortcut anymore. The public Goldsky orderbook subgraph froze at the 2026-04-28 V1->V2 migration and never indexed V2, so for any window after that date you MUST hit raw RPC. (Pre-migration windows could use the subgraph.)
- Per window you must: (a) map start/end timestamp -> block range (binary search over eth_getBlockByNumber), (b) paginate eth_getLogs (1rpc caps at 50 blocks; our window ~150 blocks = ~3 calls), (c) pull ALL exchange OrderFilled logs (~3,700 per 50 blocks) and filter client-side by tokenId because tokenId is non-indexed, (d) decode side/amounts/fee, (e) dedupe the maker+taker double-emit if you want trade-level not leg-level. Free public RPCs are rate-limited and some (polygon-rpc.com, ankr, publicnode, drpc) were dead or timed out — only 1rpc.io/matic reliably served log queries.
- An archive node isn't strictly required for recent windows (these are ~18k blocks back, within most full nodes' retention), but for older windows you'd need archive access, which free public endpoints often won't give.

Why data-api /trades is better for the actual goal:
- One GET, no key, no block math, no pagination-by-block, no client-side token filtering, already decoded (side/price/size/outcome/timestamp/tx), already trade-level. For our window it returned 974 in-window trades with both outcomes.
- The ONE thing data-api lacks that on-chain has: an explicit per-fill `fee` field, and arguably finer granularity (raw logs expose both legs and the exact maker/taker addresses + orderHash). If you need fees, maker/taker order hashes, or want to independently audit data-api, go on-chain.

Recommendation: use data-api /trades as the primary backfill source; use eth_getLogs (1rpc.io, V2 exchange, topic0 above) only as ground-truth spot-check / for fee data, or for windows where you distrust the API. Do NOT rely on the public Goldsky subgraph for anything after 2026-04-28.

NOTES:

websocket.book_schema:
LIVE-VERIFIED on an active btc-updown-5m market (token 2789...110, market 0xa73a70...87fc).

book (full L2 resting-depth SNAPSHOT — one frame PER asset_id on subscribe, and re-sent whenever a trade rewrites the book):
{
  "event_type": "book",
  "asset_id":   "<token_id string>",
  "market":     "0x<conditionId>",
  "bids":       [ {"price": "0.01", "size": "21862.98"}, {"price": "0.02", "size": "2077.5"}, ... ],   // live: 44 levels
  "asks":       [ {"price": "0.99", "size": "21349.98"}, {"price": "0.98", "size": "2047.5"}, ... ],   // live: 43 levels
  "tick_size":  "0.01",            // present live, undocumented
  "last_trade_price": "",          // present live (empty string if none yet), undocumented
  "hash":       "c7f19c6c76eff79c62446fbf9e6996f245d06c58",   // book-state checksum (note: NO 0x prefix in live data)
  "timestamp":  "1781785196281"    // STRING, unix MILLISECONDS
}
price/size are decimal STRINGS. Observed ordering: bids ASCENDING by price, asks DESCENDING by price (i.e. best bid = last bid entry, best ask = last ask entry); do NOT assume best-first — sort defensively when computing top-of-book. The full bids+asks arrays ARE the complete resting L2 depth — exactly the data not available via /prices-history. This WS book schema matches the REST GET clob.polymarket.com/book?token_id=<id> shape (same market/asset_id/timestamp/hash/bids/asks/min_order_size/tick_size/neg_risk/last_trade_price fields), so REST /book can seed/resync the same structure.

price_change (LIVE-VERIFIED — incremental DELTA; one envelope can update MULTIPLE tokens):
{
  "event_type": "price_change",
  "market":     "0x<conditionId>",
  "price_changes": [
    {
      "asset_id": "40522...688",
      "price":    "0.01",          // the price LEVEL that changed (decimal string)
      "size":     "21359.98",      // NEW absolute resting size at that level; "0" => level REMOVED
      "side":     "BUY",           // BUY => bid side, SELL => ask side
      "hash":     "d5007d3a...efe2",
      "best_bid": "0.49",          // top-of-book after this change (token's own price)
      "best_ask": "0.5"
    },
    { "asset_id": "2789...110", "price": "0.99", "size": "21359.98", "side": "SELL", "hash": "7a9f...e95d", "best_bid": "0.5", "best_ask": "0.51" }
  ],
  "timestamp": "1781785206974"     // STRING, unix MILLISECONDS, one per envelope
}
Delta semantics: for each entry, set book[side][price] = size as an ABSOLUTE replacement (not a +/- increment); if size == "0", delete that level. best_bid/best_ask are convenience top-of-book snapshots and should match your recomputed top after applying the delta (use to validate).

last_trade_price (from official docs; did not fire in the test windows because these markets sit at ~0.50 mid with no trades until the final minute):
{ "event_type":"last_trade_price", "asset_id":"<id>", "market":"0x..", "price":"<string>", "side":"BUY|SELL", "size":"<string>", "fee_rate_bps":"<string>", "timestamp":"<ms string>" }

tick_size_change (from official docs; fires when price crosses >0.96 or <0.04):
{ "event_type":"tick_size_change", "asset_id":"<id>", "market":"0x..", "old_tick_size":"<string>", "new_tick_size":"<string>", "timestamp":"<ms string>" }
websocket.collector_design:
FORWARD-ONLY L2 collector for the 5-min windows:

1) WINDOW DISCOVERY (poll gamma): GET https://gamma-api.polymarket.com/markets?closed=false&order=startDate&ascending=false , filter slug contains "updown-5m"; read clobTokenIds (= [yes_token, no_token]) and conditionId. Markets open ~20h early, so enqueue each window and schedule its collector. (Live-confirmed: returns active 5m windows with acceptingOrders=true and their clobTokenIds.)

2) CONNECT + SUBSCRIBE: open wss://ws-subscriptions-clob.polymarket.com/ws/market ; send {"assets_ids":[yes_token,no_token],"type":"market"} (batch many windows' tokens into one socket — verified working with 6 ids). Record local connect wall-clock (ms) as recv_ts.

3) SNAPSHOT: the first frame per asset_id is a `book` snapshot = full resting bid/ask depth. Initialize an in-memory book per asset_id: bids = {price->size}, asks = {price->size}. Store the server `timestamp` (ms) and `hash`. Optionally seed from REST GET clob.polymarket.com/book?token_id=<id> at the exact window-open second to guarantee t0 depth even if you connect a hair late (same schema).

4) APPLY DELTAS: on each `price_change`, for every entry: book[ side=="BUY"?bids:asks ][price] = size (absolute replace); delete level if size=="0". Server `timestamp` is ms; capture local recv_ts too. After applying, recompute best_bid/best_ask and assert they equal the entry's best_bid/best_ask (sanity check; on mismatch, resync via REST /book). On a `book` frame mid-stream (trade rewrote the book), REPLACE the whole side from the snapshot rather than delta-merging.

5) PERSIST (append-only, idempotent): write each event as one row/line: {recv_ts_ms, server_ts_ms, event_type, market, asset_id, hash, side?, price?, size?, best_bid?, best_ask?, full_book_levels? }. For `book` store the entire bids/asks arrays; for `price_change` store the per-level delta (and optionally a periodic full-book checkpoint, e.g. every N deltas or every 5s, so backtests can rebuild depth at any instant without replaying from t0). Key on (asset_id, server_ts_ms, hash) to dedupe reconnects. Persist to a tick store / partitioned parquet by window slug.

6) RESILIENCE: keep socket alive; the server may send protocol ping frames — reply with pong (also fine to proactively send a ping/pong every ~5-10s per docs). On disconnect, reconnect and the next `book` frame re-snapshots; mark a gap. Because each window only gets interesting in its final ~60-120s (sits at ~0.50 mid before that), prioritize CPU/disk for the [open, open+300s] band but keep recording the whole life so you capture the pre-resolution depth build-up. Always store BOTH outcome tokens so YES+NO depth (and the price = 1-other invariant) is reconstructable.

7) BACKTEST FIDELITY: with full book snapshots + ms-timestamped deltas you can reconstruct the exact resting L2 bid/ask depth at any millisecond inside the 5-min window — the precise thing /prices-history (1-min mid only, 5 points/window) and the data-api trades feed (executions only, no resting depth) cannot give you.

fill_model.fill_rule:
DEFINITION OF EXECUTABLE: A resting BUY is a passive bid that fills only when a SELLER crosses it. On Polymarket the tape's `price` is the traded token's OWN price and `side` is the aggressor/taker side relative to that token. The print that PROVES marketable liquidity existed at-or-below our bid is therefore the SELL print: a SELL @ p means a taker hit a resting bid at p, so the book was bid at p and any resting bid >= p (including ours at T) would have been hit first by price-time priority. A BUY @ p means a taker LIFTED an ask at p; it proves an ASK existed at p but says nothing about whether a SELLER would have reached down to our bid — using BUY prints to fill a resting BUY is the classic look-ahead/optimism error and is FORBIDDEN.

CANONICAL FILL RULE (per token, per window): Our resting BUY at threshold T fills at the timestamp of the FIRST in-window SELL print on that token whose price p <= T. Fill price = T (we are the resting order; we get our limit, not the print price — the taker's marketable sell swept through prices >= our bid and ours executes AT our posted T, never better, conservatively). Equivalently, define the token's executable-ask proxy as the running min over SELL-print prices (see price_series_construction) and fill when that proxy <= T.

WHY SELL NOT BUY: empirically YES first crosses T=0.45 via a SELL @0.18 at t=915 (a bid was that low), with the first sub-T BUY @0.13 only at t=918. A book-true fill triggers on the SELL evidence. NO never prints below 0.72 on either side, so a resting NO BUY @0.45 NEVER fills — correctly capturing that the winning side stays expensive.

EDGE CASES: (1) Same price exactly == T counts as a fill (<=). (2) If only BUY prints exist at <= T and zero SELL prints at <= T, the conservative rule = NO FILL (we cannot prove a seller would have reached us); an optimistic variant may fill but must be flagged as a bias (see biases). (3) Settlement-tail prints (t > window_end) are excluded before evaluation. (4) Both-leg arb is declared ONLY if YES fills at T_yes AND NO fills at T_no under this same SELL-print rule and T_yes+T_no < 1.00; given the complementary-price structure this is rare and that rarity is the point.
fill_model.price_series_construction:
PER-TOKEN TICK STREAM (one stream per token = YES and NO, never a synthesized single-asset ask): 

1. Filter the tape to in-window prints for that token: window_start <= timestamp <= window_end, drop settlement tail t > window_end.
2. Sort by timestamp ascending. Coarse second granularity (974 trades over 57 distinct seconds here) means many same-second prints; within a second sort SELL-before-BUY is NOT assumed — instead collapse each second to the WORST-for-us aggregate (see tie-break) so intra-second order never leaks future info.
3. Build the EXECUTABLE-ASK PROXY from SELL prints only: ask_proxy(t) = running minimum of SELL-print prices seen up to and including t. This is monotone non-increasing and is the price a resting BUY can be proven hittable at. (Symmetrically, an executable-BID proxy = running max of BUY prints, used only if you ever model resting SELLs.) Emit a Tick whenever a SELL print arrives that lowers the running min; that Tick carries (timestamp, ask_proxy=price, aggressor_size=size).
4. The engine consumes this as a monotone Tick stream and fills the resting BUY on the first Tick with ask_proxy <= T.

TEMPORAL DOUBLE-DIP PRESERVED: because YES and NO are INDEPENDENT streams with their own timestamps, the two legs cross T at DIFFERENT seconds (or one never crosses). YES arms at its first sub-T SELL (t=915 here); NO would arm only at its own first sub-T SELL (never, here). The model must place/evaluate both resting orders for the WHOLE window and let each fill on its own clock — do NOT require simultaneity. A second "dip" later in the window (price drops again) is naturally captured because the running-min proxy keeps emitting lower Ticks; if the strategy re-arms or sizes across multiple dips, each qualifying Tick is a separate fill opportunity at the same T. The double-dip is thus two legs at two different times, plus optionally multiple fills per leg across successive lower Ticks.

CRITICAL: do not interpolate or forward-fill mid between sparse prints — the first ~4 minutes have ZERO prints; treating that void as a tradable 0.50 mid is fictitious. No print = no executable evidence = no fill in that interval.
fill_model.lookahead_safety:
1. STRICTLY CAUSAL EVALUATION: the engine processes Ticks in non-decreasing timestamp order and may only consult prints with timestamp <= current sim clock. A fill decision at time t uses the running-min SELL proxy computed from [window_start, t] ONLY. No future print, no min-over-whole-window peek.

2. TIMESTAMPS MUST BE NON-DECREASING AND DEDUPED ACROSS SAME SECOND: sort ascending by timestamp; for equal timestamps, since true order is unknowable at second granularity, evaluate all same-second SELL prints as one batch but apply the conservative resolution (a same-second SELL <= T arms the fill at that second, never earlier). Never let a same-second BUY that lifted an ask retroactively imply an earlier fill.

3. SETTLEMENT-TAIL EXCLUSION (mandatory): prints with t > window_end are post-resolution convergence (here SELL @0.99 / @0.01 at t=1781756999, the last second). They reflect the known outcome and MUST be dropped before building the proxy, else the model 'fills' on a price that only exists because the result is already public — direct resolution leak. Apply a small guard band: also scrutinize the final 1-2 seconds inside the window for convergence-to-{0,1} prints and treat them as outcome leakage candidates.

4. NO RESOLUTION FIELD ANYWHERE IN THE FILL PATH: the fill engine consumes only (timestamp, price, side, size). conditionId resolution / winning outcome is read ONLY by the PnL accounting AFTER fills are decided, never as an input to whether/when a leg fills.

5. NO DEPTH/BOOK INPUT: by construction we have no resting book, so there is no future-order leakage — the only temporal data is the causal tape, which the running-min enforces.
fill_model.size_handling:
We never see resting depth, only realized taker volume, so fillable size must be PROXIED from print size with an explicit conservative/optimistic toggle:

CONSERVATIVE (recommended default): our fill size on a qualifying SELL Tick is capped at min(our_requested_size, participation_fraction * that_print's_size). Rationale: a SELL print of size s proves >= s of bid liquidity was consumed at p; we could realistically have captured only a fraction because we'd be queued behind other resting bids at >= p (price-time priority) and other takers compete. Use participation_fraction in [0.1, 0.5] (default 0.25). Multiple qualifying Ticks accumulate fill until requested size is met. If total proven SELL volume <= T across the window < requested size, we get a PARTIAL fill = realistic.

OPTIMISTIC (sensitivity bound only): assume infinite depth at the proxy price — any SELL print <= T fills our full requested size instantly. Use ONLY to compute an upper PnL bound; never as the production default.

QUEUE-POSITION HAIRCUT: because we are resting, even the conservative cap overstates fills when many bids sit at the same tick. A second-order refinement is to subtract an assumed ahead-of-us queue (e.g. require cumulative sub-T SELL volume to exceed an assumed queue Q before our fill starts). Default Q=0 for v1, exposed as a knob.

DOLLAR-NOTIONAL SANITY: cap per-window deployed capital at a fixed bankroll slice so a single thin window with one tiny print can't be levered into an unrealistic position.
bias_warnings: Printed-price-as-fill-proxy bias: we assume our resting BUY executes at exactly T, but SELL prints occurred at prices p<<T (YES SELLs down to 0.01). A real resting bid at T would have been the FIRST to be hit and filled AT T, so executing at T is correct-conservative on price but ignores that we'd be queued behind cheaper/earlier bids — may overstate fill probability.

Survivorship / crossed-order bias: we only observe trades that CLEARED. Quotes that rested at our T but were never hit leave no print, so we systematically undercount available liquidity at T (understate fills); conversely we never see orders that were cancelled before execution (overstate, if we naively count a print as guaranteed-our-fill).

BUY-print contamination: if an implementer wrongly arms resting BUYs on BUY prints (ask lifts), fills become wildly optimistic and look-ahead-unsafe — a BUY @0.13 does not prove a seller would reach our 0.45 bid.

Back-loaded-tape / empty-window bias: 100% of prints fall in the last ~85s (t>=915 of a 300s window); the first 4 minutes have no executable evidence. Models that forward-fill a 0.50 mid will fabricate fills that the tape cannot support — and conversely, a genuinely fillable early quote that simply wasn't traded is invisible (understated).
Settlement-convergence leak: prints at/after window_end snap to 0.99/0.01 because the outcome is decided; including them fills legs on post-resolution prices = direct look-ahead. Must be excised.

Asymmetric-crossing selection bias: only the LOSING side gets cheap (YES->0 here) while the winning side (NO) stays >0.72 and never crosses T. So single-leg fills are overwhelmingly on the side that settles to $0 -> the unhedged-fill PnL distribution is adversely selected (you tend to buy the loser cheap). The fill model is correct to fill mostly the loser; the STRATEGY-level danger is mistaking 'cheap' for 'value'.

Same-second ordering bias: 974 trades over 57 seconds means intra-second sequence is unknown; any rule that orders within a second injects look-ahead. Batch-per-second conservative resolution avoids it but slightly delays/penalizes fills.

Size-from-volume bias: taker print size is a lower bound on resting depth, not our fillable quantity; both the conservative fraction and the optimistic infinite-depth assumption are guesses, so position sizes carry wide error bars.
fill_model.recommended_default: DEFAULT MODEL = 'Causal running-min SELL-proxy, fill-at-T, conservative fractional size.' Per token build a Tick stream from in-window SELL prints only (drop t>window_end settlement tail), maintain ask_proxy = running min of SELL-print prices, and fill the resting BUY at the first Tick where ask_proxy <= T, executing AT price T for size = min(requested, 0.25 * triggering_print_size) accumulated across qualifying Ticks. Evaluate YES and NO as independent streams so each leg fills on its own clock (temporal double-dip), declaring locked arb only when both fill with T_yes+T_no<1. WHY: it is the unique rule that (a) uses only proven marketable liquidity (SELL = someone hit a bid), (b) is strictly causal / look-ahead-safe by running-min + tail exclusion, (c) reproduces the observed asymmetry (loser fills, winner doesn't) without fabricating fills in the empty early window, and (d) is conservative on both price (fill at limit T, not the deeper print) and size (fractional participation). Ship the optimistic infinite-depth + BUY-print variants as sensitivity bounds only, never as production.
fill_model.comparison_to_mid: The current mid+half_spread reconstruction is materially wrong for THIS strategy for four compounding reasons. (1) Resolution / sparsity: prices-history gives only ~5 one-minute mid points in a 300s window and the real tape shows ALL activity compressed into the final 85s; a 1-min mid linearly bridges a void at ~0.50 and would 'fill' a 0.45 resting bid in minute 1-4 where ZERO executable liquidity existed. The trade-tape model fills only when a SELL print proves a hittable bid. (2) Direction-blindness: mid+half_spread is symmetric and outcome-agnostic, so it fills YES and NO roughly together near 0.50, manufacturing phantom locked-arb. The tape shows the truth: YES collapses toward 0 (fills) while NO stays >0.72 (never fills) — the legs cross T at different times or not at all, which only a per-token SELL-print stream captures. (3) Spread fiction: half_spread is a guessed constant; the tape gives the actual price a counterparty transacted at, and the SELL/BUY tag tells us which side was marketable — information a mid simply does not contain. (4) Look-ahead: a mid series interpolated across the window implicitly encodes the endpoint (near-resolution) value into earlier timestamps, leaking the outcome backward; the causal running-min over real prints with settlement-tail exclusion cannot. Net: mid+half_spread overstates arb frequency, mis-times fills, and is not look-ahead-safe; the SELL-proxy tape model fills only on proven, causally-available liquidity and reproduces the real loser-fills/winner-doesn't asymmetry.
